questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to prioritize maximum image quality or assign a recognizable filename for your own records.
questions.verify_form: The agent picked PNG-at-100 or JPEG-at-70 - check the format against fidelity and file size; the choice is baked into the pixels.

questions.question: Did the image export as a standard, universally compatible file format like PNG or JPG rather than a web-optimized format like WEBP?
questions.why: Browsers and some web-based AI tools default to saving images as WEBP or AVIF, which might not be compatible with the user's downstream editing software or publishing platform.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might deliver a file format that the user cannot open or use in their intended workflow, requiring a manual format conversion later.

questions.question: How do you download the image and confirm the file saved successfully?
questions.why: Verifying the completion notification after clicking download ensures the file was successfully saved to your local device.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of personally verifying the download completion notification and file size.

questions.question: Does the browser confirm the download after you click the button?
questions.why: The narrator stated the action would download the artwork, and the browser's download confirmation verifies that the file was successfully saved.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the visual certainty that the final image file was actually saved to your local machine.

questions.question: Does the file size of the saved image match the size shown when uploaded to imglarger.com?
questions.why: The Windows file properties dialog showed the saved image size as 3.43 MB, but the imglarger.com interface displayed the uploaded file size as 3.60 MB.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to confirm that the exact same file was transferred without any hidden alterations or measurement discrepancies.

questions.question: Does the exported image actually have a transparent alpha channel, or did the AI just draw a fake checkerboard background?
questions.why: When prompted for a 'transparent background', AI tools often struggle and will literally draw a grey-and-white checkerboard pattern instead of creating an actual transparent PNG.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might deliver an image that it claims fulfills the 'no background' prompt, leaving you with a useless solid image containing a fake transparency grid.

questions.question: Which recent chat in the sidebar contains the image sequence you want to open?
questions.why: The left sidebar lists several recent conversations like 'Futuristic Cityscape Image' and 'New chat', requiring you to remember which vaguely named thread holds the specific images you need.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent lacks your personal memory of which vaguely named chat session actually contains the specific creative context you intended to build upon.

questions.question: Which tab should you open to manage past creations or access the workspace?
questions.why: The sidebar provides options like 'Creations' and 'Canvas', which determine whether you review previous work or start in a larger workspace.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to choose the most suitable interface for their current creative needs.
questions.verify_form: The agent opened Creations or Canvas - check where it took the work; review against workspace are different next steps.

questions.question: Which generated images and prompts should you save to your library for future use?
questions.why: Hovering over the generated images reveals 'Save to Library' and 'Copy Prompt' icons, allowing you to easily preserve the best variations and their text parameters.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might only export the final requested image, missing the chance to curate your account's library with inspiring intermediate results and reusable prompts.
questions.verify_form: The agent saved (or didn't) candidates and prompts to the library - check what got kept; the curation of your account was its call.

questions.question: Should I save this candidate to a collection before moving on?
questions.why: The screen shows the large view of a generated image with a Save button that allows adding it to a collection.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to personally curate and organize their favorite generated images into specific collections.
questions.verify_form: The agent saved (or skipped saving) the candidate to a collection - check the keep matches what you'd shelve.

questions.question: Should you open the completed 'female alchemist' generation from the notifications dropdown?
questions.why: The notifications menu shows an image generation completed 13 minutes ago, providing a shortcut to review those specific results.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to choose whether to revisit a recently completed generation or continue focusing on the current task.
questions.verify_form: The agent opened (or ignored) the finished generation in notifications - check nothing completed got forgotten.

questions.question: Where should you navigate to view your own generated images?
questions.why: The sidebar presents multiple options like "Community Feed" and "AI Image Generation", making it necessary to select "Personal Feed" to find your specific outputs.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user misses the chance to explore community creations for inspiration or discover other available tools in the sidebar.

questions.question: Does the generation history accurately display all the images you created during this session?
questions.why: The timeline shows older and newer creations but is missing the four whale vector images generated in between, indicating a potential sync or display issue.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to retrieve, review, or iterate on specific past generations if the tool fails to save them to the history.

questions.question: Where do you go to access the finished video?
questions.why: The generation dialog explicitly directs the user to check the AI Gen page or the Library to find their completed media.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to review the automatic pan and zoom effect applied to their image before the final MP4 is downloaded.

questions.question: Do you verify that the generated motion video appears in the Library as indicated?
questions.why: The 'Generating Motion' dialog states the video can be viewed in the Library when complete, making this check necessary to confirm the generation was successful.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the confirmation that their final animated asset was properly saved and is accessible for download.

questions.question: Does your current subscription tier grant commercial usage rights for this exported image?
questions.why: Free tiers on many AI platforms explicitly restrict generated images to personal, non-commercial use, which violates the terms of service if your concrete goal is for a business, logo, or monetized project.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might generate and deliver a perfect logo on a free account, leaving you legally exposed and violating platform terms if you actually use it commercially.
